title: Triangle closure for complete complexes with finite étale residue origin
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with its fixed small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, and finite residue field $\kappa=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and work in the ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For $K$ in this category let $K_1=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}\kappa_X$, using the derived tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], with its $\kappa_X$-module structure from derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Say $P(K)$ if $K$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and $K_1\cong\nu_X^*A$ for a bounded étale complex $A$ with constructible cohomology, where $\nu_X^*$ and bounded constructible étale complexes are as explicitly defined in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Then $P(0)$ holds, $P$ is invariant under isomorphisms, and $P(K[n])\Longleftrightarrow P(K)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. For every ambient distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$, any two of $P(K),P(L),P(M)$ imply the third. In particular if $P(K)$ and $P(M)$ hold, then $L$ is derived complete and $L_1$ has bounded constructible étale origin. No Noetherian, dimension, finite-type or invertibility hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison] with $R=R_X$ and $\pi=\pi_E$. It gives an additive completion functor $F$ and its natural map $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$, with completeness equivalent to invertibility of $c_K$. Since $F$ is additive, $F(0)$ is zero, so $c_0$ is an isomorphism. For an isomorphism $u:K\to L$, naturality gives $c_L=F(u)c_Ku^{-1}$; hence completeness is invariant under isomorphisms. For every integer $n$, the identity $\sigma_{K,n}c_{K[n]}=c_K[n]$ and invertibility of $\sigma_{K,n}$ show that $K[n]$ is complete if and only if $K$ is complete. No boundedness of $K$ is used.

source.place: Cones and shifts paragraphs: the canonical completion map and its shift comparison; applied to the first sentence of paragraph (1) of the item source.

proof.text: For an ambient distinguished triangle $T=(K\to L\to M\to K[1])$, [lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison] makes $(c_K,c_L,c_M)$ a morphism from $T$ to the distinguished triangle $F(T)$, including the last square involving $c_K[1]$. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], invertibility of any two of these three maps implies invertibility of the third. The completeness criterion from step 1 therefore gives the required two-out-of-three assertion for completeness alone.

source.place: Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle, applied to the completion triangle morphism of the preceding source.

proof.text: The coefficient map $R_X\to\kappa_X$ is a map of commutative ring sheaves on the same fixed small site. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], clause (2), to obtain the exact derived scalar-extension functor $T_1:D(R_X)\to D(\kappa_X)$, $T_1(K)=K_1$, retaining its $\kappa_X$-module structure. Thus $T_1$ carries the given ambient triangle to a distinguished triangle of $\kappa_X$-modules, and its shift comparisons identify $T_1(K[n])$ with $K_1[n]$. Exact functors are additive, so $T_1(0)$ is zero, and every functor preserves isomorphisms. Next identify the residue coefficient ring. By [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence], applied to the finite commutative ring $\kappa$ with its discrete condensed structure, the pulled-back ring $\kappa_X=p_X^*\underline\kappa$ over which $K_1$ is formed is isomorphic as a ring object to the constant ring sheaf of $\kappa$, and its module objects are exactly equivalent to ordinary module sheaves over that constant ring, by a termwise derived equivalence preserving shifts and distinguished triangles. The coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] for $\Lambda=\kappa$ is the same ring: the map from the constant presheaf $\kappa$ to $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\kappa)$ is locally surjective, since a continuous function to the finite discrete set $\kappa$ is constant on each member of the Zariski covering of $U$ by its clopen fibres, and locally injective, since distinct constants differ on every nonempty $U$ and an empty $U$ is covered by the empty family; so it becomes an isomorphism after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Below, $\kappa_X$ and $T_1$ are read through these identifications.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for the identity underlying topos with the coefficient map; compare Tag 06YU and the K-flat change-of-rings construction. Residue ring identification: sites-modules.tex Tag 093I (constant sheaves) and the cited module-object comparison.

proof.text: In the residue category use the ordinary constant finite ring sheaf $\kappa_X$ and the termwise exact comparison $\nu_X^*$ specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. When applying the fixed-module-valued comparison results below, use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-encoding]: restriction to constant scalars is an equivalence and leaves the underlying additive sheaf unchanged. The inverse extends constant scalar actions locally along the sheafification unit; hence on an étale pullback both descriptions have the same scalar action, determined by their constant sections. This identifies the two comparison functors. The equivalence preserves zero, kernels and cokernels by their universal properties; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] therefore give its termwise derived equivalence and its cohomology identifications. Constant module sheaves, finite stalks and restrictions to each stratum are unchanged: all their scalar-linear maps are the same maps after restriction to constant scalars. In particular the global finite-stratification predicates in the fixed-module comparison nodes are precisely the ordinary constant-ring-sheaf predicates used here. This step changes no integral coefficient ring and uses no constructibility theorem for condensed integral modules.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 093I, constant scalar restriction and module sheafification; homology.tex Tag 010N and derived.tex Tag 015F for the exact equivalence on complexes.

proof.text:
For $N\in D(\kappa_X)$ let $Q(N)$ mean that its cohomology vanishes outside a finite integer interval and each cohomology sheaf is intrinsically globally constructible. If $N\cong
u_X^*A$ with $A$ bounded constructible étale, exactness of the inverse image and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] give $H^i(N)\cong
u_X^*H^i(A)$, with the same vanishing interval. The forward construction in [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-constructible-origin] makes each of these sheaves constructible. Conversely, if $Q(N)$ holds, that same node supplies a globally constructible étale antecedent for each $H^i(N)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-bounded-constructible-origin] to the bounded complex $N$ and these antecedents. It supplies an étale derived object $A$ with bounded globally constructible cohomology and $N\cong
u_X^*A$. Step 4 identifies its coefficient convention with ours. Consequently $Q(N)$ is equivalent to the condition of being isomorphic to the inverse image of a bounded étale complex with constructible cohomology. All these comparison statements allow arbitrary schemes and finite commutative coefficient rings; here $\kappa$ is a finite field.

source.place: Tags 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible) and 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived), with the global finite-stratification comparison and bounded reconstruction stated in the two cited fixed-module nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] with $Y=X$ and $\Lambda=\kappa$. It says exactly that $Q$ contains zero, is invariant under isomorphisms and integer shifts, and is closed under extensions in ambient distinguished triangles. To spell out the remaining positions, if $Q(N_1)$ and $Q(N_2)$ hold for a distinguished triangle $N_1\to N_2\to N_3\to N_1[1]$, rotate it to $N_2\to N_3\to N_1[1]\to N_2[1]$ and apply extension closure. If instead $Q(N_2)$ and $Q(N_3)$ hold, rotate twice, obtaining $N_3\to N_1[1]\to N_2[1]\to N_3[1]$, apply extension closure and shift back. These rotations are distinguished by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus any two imply the third. Using the equivalence in step 5, the same statements hold for the bounded constructible étale-origin condition.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, proof: the constructible cohomology subcategories are triangulated; its bounded form is the cited node. Rotations: derived.tex Tag 0145, TR2.

proof.text: The predicate $P(K)$ is the conjunction of completeness and $Q(T_1(K))$ by step 5. Steps 1, 3 and 6 give $P(0)$, isomorphism invariance, and $P(K[n])\Longleftrightarrow P(K)$ for every integer $n$. Given a distinguished triangle and any two of its $P$ assertions, step 2 supplies completeness of the third vertex; step 3 reduces the triangle and step 6 supplies $Q$ at its third vertex. Step 5 converts this back to bounded constructible étale origin. This proves every two-out-of-three implication. In particular completeness and the required residue origin hold for $L$ when $P(K)$ and $P(M)$ hold. None of the steps imposes a Noetherian, dimension, finite-type, or invertibility hypothesis on $X$.
